newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares up with bonds on Yeltsin, economy.
newsitem.headline: German shares up with bonds on Yeltsin, economy.

text.p: German shares finished strongly highly on Tuesday, boosted by German government bonds which had risen on reports that Russian President Boris Yeltsin's heart operation had been successfully completed.
The release of lower German industrial orders in September, data taken as suggesting that there was no need to rein back the economy with higher interest rates, also helped German debt prices higher.
The DAX index of 30 leading shares closed floor trade up 19.43 points, or 0.73 percent, at 2,691.29.
The IBIS DAX index of all-day computer dealings in the DAX index later climbed above the crucial 2,700 point level to close up 37.43 points at 2,716.16.
But dealers said overall trade was thin as the market held back ahead of the results of the U.S, election.

Although Democrat U.S. President Bill Clinton is widely expected to win a second term, markets are watching to see whether the Republicans can hold onto their majority in the House of Representatives.
If the Democrats win a majority in the House, they are seen pursuing a less strict budget policy than the Republicans, which would worry markets.
"If everything in the U.S. stays the same than the market could be stronger, otherwise we could test the lows from last week around 2,660 points," said one trader.
He said if in the unlikely case Republican Bob Dole won the Presidency, then the market would also react negatively. "Dole is a weak character. We don't need an ill man in Washington too."
The day's biggest loser amongst the DAX stocks was Germany's largest bank Deutsche Bank, which is due to hold an analysts' meeting on Wednesday.

Traders said there had probably been a large sell order from a foreign investor and the fact the stock had dropped below the technical and psychological level of 70 marks had also weighed on the stock.
Deutsche ended bourse dealings down 53 pfennigs at 69.77 marks.
Chemicals group BASF saw its shares jump to a day-high after it announced a deal under which South Korea's Kohap group would buy its ailing magnetic tape products business for an undisclosed sum.
Its shares rose to a day-high of 50.25 marks on the new, then fell back to trade up 78 pfennigs, or 1.6 percent, at 50.04 marks.
